description: Account status: whether this session is connected to a 包租公 · YieldLord account, which tier it is on, how many credits are left, and for Gold whether it is a trial or paid and when it ends. Call this when the user asks "am I connected" or "how many credits do I have left", and when they ask about THEIR OWN positions, portfolio, morning brief or realized history — anonymous access cannot see those, and this explains what connecting unlocks and gives the link. Called with no arguments it returns text and a URL only. Call it again with start_authorization=true once the user has an account, to begin the OAuth flow — or, if you can't receive a browser redirect, with start_link=true (a link the user approves, then pickup=<pickup> gives you the token; nothing to copy back). A connected free account can also start its free Gold trial here (start_trial=true — always a two-step confirm with the user) or get the link to buy Gold. Call it again right after the user finishes signing in: for a connected account the reply lists every tool the connection unlocked (the tool list you fetched before sign-in only has the public ones — re-list tools after connecting).

agent_name.description: With start_link: your name as the user knows you (shown on the approval page).

confirm.description: The confirm_token from the previous start_trial call, sent only after the user said yes.

pickup.description: The pickup from start_link. Returns pending until the user approves, then the access token (once).

start_authorization.description: Begin the OAuth flow now. The call answers HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header pointing at this server's protected-resource metadata; follow it (dynamic client registration, PKCE S256, public client, no secret) and give the user the sign-in link to approve. Use it only after the user has an account — a plain link cannot open the authorize page, because that URL needs your own client_id, redirect_uri and code_challenge. If you can't receive a browser redirect (you run on a server, not on the user's computer), register this server's /api/mcp/callback page as your redirect_uri — the user copies the full URL from it back to you.

start_link.description: Easiest way to connect if you can't receive a browser redirect (you run on a server): returns a link and a code to give the user, plus a pickup for you. The user signs in and approves on that page — nothing to copy back. Then call again with pickup=<pickup> to receive the access token.

start_trial.description: Connected free accounts only: start the free Gold trial. Without `confirm` nothing is started — it returns a question for the user and a confirm_token. Ask the user; only after they clearly say yes, call again with start_trial=true and confirm=<confirm_token>. Never confirm on the user's behalf.

name: connect_my_account
